page: Amazon Web Services m7g.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors utilizing the ARM64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores based on the Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture, running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz with a single thread per core. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. No local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths are strong, reaching 237.87 GB/sec and 109.3 GB/sec respectively. In compute tasks, the instance delivers average single-core and multi-core performance in stress-ng tests. Database operations and static web serving throughput are strong, with web serving reaching 49.88 GB/sec. However, large language model inference tasks show mixed results, with text generation on small models and prompt processing on large models performing poorly.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64-based Graviton architecture offers high resource density and power efficiency compared to traditional x86 architectures, translating to lower operational costs for general-purpose workloads. The absence of local storage means storage-heavy workloads must rely on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. This instance is highly suited for application servers, multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, and containerized microservices that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high memory bandwidth.
